title: Adenoid removal
what: An ENT doctor removes overgrown tissue behind the nose that blocks breathing. It is done through the mouth, with no cuts on the face, usually under general anesthesia.
why: When a child always breathes through the mouth, snores, often gets ear infections, or hears worse because of the adenoids.
duration: surgery usually takes 20 to 40 minutes; children usually go home the same day or the next day
tell_doctor: If your child had a cold in the last 2 to 4 weeks. Surgery is often postponed
If your child or relatives had bleeding problems or problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, sometimes an ECG and a check by the pediatrician. Your clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Anesthesiologist
prepare.text: Before surgery, an anesthesiologist will talk with you. Tell them about your child's health.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually your child cannot eat from the evening before, or drink for a few hours before. Your clinic will give you the exact times.

prepare.title: Talking
prepare.text: Calmly explain to your child that they will sleep, and then their nose will breathe better.

bring: Your child's and your own ID documents
A change of clothes and water to drink after surgery
steps: Your child changes clothes. Sometimes an IV is put into a vein
In the operating room, the anesthesiologist gives the anesthesia, and your child falls asleep
The doctor removes the adenoids through the mouth
Your child wakes up in the ward. A parent can usually be nearby
A few hours later, the doctor checks your child
feel: After anesthesia: sleepiness, sometimes nausea or crankiness
A stuffy nose and a slightly nasal voice. This will pass
The throat or ears may hurt a little
after: For a few days, soft, warm food, not hot
Usually 1 to 2 weeks with no hot baths, sauna, sun, or sports. The doctor will tell you how long
Bad breath and a slight fever can happen in the first days
Nose drops and care as your doctor advises
red_flags: Bleeding from the nose or mouth that does not stop: call emergency services
Fever above 38.5 degrees, or your child refuses to drink

faq.a: Sometimes, but not often. It happens more in young children. The doctor will explain the risks for your child.

faq.q: Do adenoids always have to be removed?
faq.a: No, not always. Often they are treated without surgery first. The ENT doctor decides on removal if the adenoids affect breathing or hearing.

reminders.text: Your child's surgery is tomorrow. Pack the documents, test results, and a toy. Food and water only until the times your clinic gave you.
